citeturn0search2 [wordlim: 200] Crawled: 2 weeks ago; Scroll edge effects work in concert with Liquid Glass to maintain that crucial separation between the UI and content layers and ensure legibility, especially with dynamically scrolling content. ... The true magic of Liquid Glass lies in its holistic design. ... First, the highlights layer Liquid Glass lives inside an environment that behaves like the world around us.
Liquid Glass uses these instinctive visual cues to provide separation and communicate layering in a new way while letting content shine through underneath it.

Where as previous materials scattered light, this new set of materials dynamically bends, shapes, and concentrates light in real time.

This provides definition against the background content while still feeling visually grounded in our experience of the natural world. By sculpting light like this, controls can feel ultra lightweight and transparent while still being visually distinguishable.

Instead of fading, Liquid Glass objects materialize in and out by gradually modulating the light bending and lensing, ensuring a graceful transition that preserves the optical integrity of the material.

How the material feels and behaves is just as important as the way it looks. From its foundation, both the visuals AND motion of LiquidGlass were designed as one. The motion of liquids is something we all have an intuitive feel for. Their smooth, responsive, and effortless motion and behavior are properties that interfaces can reference to move and react in a way that aligns with our innate grasp of the physical world.

To this effect, Liquid Glass responds to interaction by instantly flexing and energizing with light.

This makes the interface feel responsive, satisfying, and alive.

And it has an inherent gel-like flexibility to it that communicates its transient and malleable nature, as it moves in tandem with your interaction. This fluidity helps the interface feel aligned with the dynamism and continually changing nature of our thinking and movement.

Elements can even lift up into Liquid Glass temporarily, such as when you interact with a component. This lets the resting state stay visually quiet, while it comes to life on touch.

This works great for things like controls, where the transparent liquid lens can be seen through to precisely observe the value underneath it.

This sense of fluidity also extends not just to how the material reacts to your input, but also how it reacts to the dynamically changing environments of modern apps. As you go between states in an app, Liquid Glass dynamically morphs between thecontrols in each context. This maintains the concept of having a singular floating plane that the controls live on. And it makes transitions between different sections of an app feel fluid and seamless, as the controls continually shape shift. When showing a menu, the bubble simply pops open to reveal the content contained within.

This lightweight, in-line transition keeps everything right where you just tapped. And it communicates a very clear and direct relationship between the button and the content contained within.

With these properties, Liquid Glass ushers in a new era of how apps look. But it also changes how they feel, too.

With the foundation in place, the next step is understanding how to structure your app to make the most of Liquid Glass.

As apps become more immersive and content-focused, the UI should support interaction where needed, and remain unobtrusive when it’s not. Liquid Glass defines a new functional layer in the UI, floating above your content to bring structure and clarity, without ever stealing focus.

One of the ways this comes to life is by clearly depicting relationships between surfaces— how they appear and stay connected to their source in a way that feels spatial yet grounded.

Take the Action Sheet. It used to appear at the bottom of the screen, no matter where the action came from. Now, it springs from the action itself, which serves as the source for the action sheet. Clearly defined roles help the system understand that relationship, anchoring the interaction as it extends directly from the tapped element.

When making custom controls, use the same approach, and make sure to apply the material directly to the control, not its inner views.

Liquid Glass helps reflect navigation focus by introducing subtle material variation that reinforces intent as navigation deepens or shifts.

While it might sound complicated, it builds on familiar cues, like using a dimming layer to signal modality when a sheet appears. When a task interrupts the main flow, pair Liquid Glass with a dimming layer to help center attention, making the sheet feel like a clear, purposeful space.

import os
from pathlib import Path

from playwright.sync_api import sync_playwright


def main():
    root = Path.cwd()
    output = root / 'workspace' / 'ui-critique'
    output.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    os.environ['RUTILE_WORKSPACE'] = str(output)
    os.environ['RUTILE_CATALOG_PATH'] = str(output / 'catalog.sqlite3')
    from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
    from rutile3.api.app import app

    with TestClient(app, base_url='http://127.0.0.1:8765') as client, sync_playwright() as p:
        browser = p.chromium.launch(channel='msedge', headless=True)
        page = browser.new_page(viewport={'width': 1440, 'height': 900}, reduced_motion='reduce')

        def forward(route):
            req = route.request
            response = client.request(req.method, req.url, content=req.post_data_buffer, headers=req.headers)
            route.fulfill(status=response.status_code, headers=dict(response.headers), body=response.content)

        page.route('http://127.0.0.1:8765/**', forward)
        page.on('pageerror', lambda error: print(error, flush=True))
        page.goto('http://127.0.0.1:8765/')

        def capture(name, full=False):
            page.evaluate('document.fonts.ready')
            print(name, page.evaluate('''() => ({viewport: innerHeight, document: document.documentElement.scrollHeight,
                window: document.querySelector('.screen:not([hidden])').getBoundingClientRect().width,
                panels: [...document.querySelectorAll('.workspace > :not([hidden]), .optimizer-panel')].filter(e=> e.offsetWidth).map(e=> [e.className, Math.round(e.getBoundingClientRect().width)])})'''), flush=True)
            page.screenshot(path=output / f'{name}.png', full_page=full)

        page.locator('#start-button').wait_for()
        capture('title')
        page.locator('#start-button').click()
        page.locator('#menu-settings').click()
        capture('settings')
        page.locator('#shell-back').click()
        page.locator('#menu-optimize').click()
        page.locator('#studio-create').click()
        page.locator('#family-al').click()
        capture('family')
        page.locator('#opt-next').click()
        page.locator('[name=opt-element][value=Cu]').check()
        page.locator('#opt-Cu-amount').fill('4')
        capture('composition', True)
        page.locator('#create-use-balance').click()
        page.locator('#opt-next').click()
        capture('processing', True)
        page.locator('#shell-back').click()
        page.locator('#shell-back').click()
        page.locator('#shell-back').click()
        page.locator('#shell-back').click()
        page.locator('#menu-diagrams').click()
        page.locator('#upload').set_input_files(root / 'examples' / 'AlCu-21Kro.tdb')
        page.locator('#calculation-settings > summary').click()
        page.locator('#temperature-mode').select_option('manual')
        page.locator('#resolution').select_option('31,25')
        capture('setup', True)
        page.locator('#calculation-settings > summary').click()
        page.locator('#calculate').click()
        page.wait_for_function("!document.querySelector('#export').disabled", timeout=180_000)
        page.locator('#plot').focus()
        page.keyboard.press('ArrowRight')
        page.keyboard.press('Enter')
        capture('diagram', True)
        page.set_viewport_size({'width': 1280, 'height': 800})
        capture('diagram-1280', True)
        page.set_viewport_size({'width': 390, 'height': 844})
        capture('diagram-mobile', True)


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

from io import BytesIO
from pathlib import Path
import base64

from PIL import Image
from playwright.sync_api import sync_playwright


def main():
    preview = Path(r'C:\Users\Joel Weikel\.codex\visualizations\2026\11\13\01a1d68f-a65c-7091-ac91-3aa08b71a1a2\rutile-workspaces.html')
    folder = Path(__file__).parent
    fragment = preview.read_text(encoding='utf-8')
    if 'ACTUAL_RUTILE_PLOT' in fragment:
        with Image.open(folder / 'diagram.png') as screenshot, BytesIO() as cropped:
            screenshot.crop((312, 292, 1160, 814)).save(cropped, 'PNG', optimize=True)
            fragment = fragment.replace('ACTUAL_RUTILE_PLOT', base64.b64encode(cropped.getvalue()).decode('ascii'))
        preview.write_text(fragment, encoding='utf-8')
    assert preview.stat().st_size < 1_000_000

    with sync_playwright() as p:
        browser = p.chromium.launch(channel='msedge', headless=True)
        page = browser.new_page(viewport={'width': 1024, 'height': 900})
        errors = []
        page.on('pageerror', lambda error: errors.append(str(error)))
        page.set_content('<meta charset="utf-8">' + fragment)
        assert page.locator('.plot img').evaluate('img => img.naturalWidth') == 848
        page.screenshot(path=folder / 'concept-diagram.png')
        page.get_by_text('Independent checks', exact=True).click()
        assert page.get_by_text('775 samples · 765 agreement', exact=False).is_visible()
        page.get_by_role('button', name='Composition', exact=True).click()
        assert page.locator('[data-balance]').inner_text() == '95 wt%'
        page.screenshot(path=folder / 'concept-composition.png')
        page.get_by_role('spinbutton', name='Cu amount in wt%').fill('9')
        assert page.locator('[data-balance]').inner_text() == '90 wt%'
        page.get_by_role('button', name='Si Silicon').click()
        assert page.locator('[data-balance]').inner_text() == '89 wt%'
        page.get_by_role('spinbutton', name='Cu amount in wt%').fill('99')
        assert page.get_by_text('Additions must leave a positive aluminum balance.').is_visible()
        page.get_by_role('spinbutton', name='Cu amount in wt%').fill('5')
        page.get_by_role('combobox', name='Composition basis').select_option('at%')
        assert page.locator('[data-balance]').inner_text() == '93 at%'
        page.set_viewport_size({'width': 320, 'height': 850})
        for name in ('Composition', 'Phase diagrams'):
            page.get_by_role('button', name=name, exact=True).click()
            assert page.evaluate('document.documentElement.scrollWidth <= innerWidth')
        assert not errors, errors
        print('Preview layout, image, basis, balance, validation, and narrow-screen checks passed.')


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

content.text:
I’d keep the title screen, crystal dive, and phase diagram styling. Inside the workspaces, I’d use **matte surfaces with shallow bevels**, and save the strongest glass and glow for navigation, the lattice, and selected elements. That gives the app some physical depth while making forms and scientific readouts easier to scan. It’s also close to Apple’s Liquid Glass guidance, which treats glass as a layer for controls over content. [Apple’s design overview](https://developer.apple.com/videos/play/wwdc2025/356/)

visualize{"path":"C:/Users/Joel Weikel/.codex/visualizations/2026/11/13/01a1d68f-a65c-7091-ac91-3aa08b71a1a2/rutile-workspaces.html","mode":"wide"}

**Phase diagrams first.** I ran Al–Cu in the browser. At 1440 × 900, the completed page was about 1,600 pixels tall even with calculation settings collapsed. On mobile, the setup still comes before the plot, and the inspector sits below the legend, checks, and provenance. Give the result a compact toolbar with **Edit setup** and **Export JSON**, put the plot first, and keep the inspector beside it on desktop and directly below it on mobile. Show disagreements and unresolved coverage in a short, visible status row with expandable details.

**Widen after Alloy Family, then use the width.** Composition already had a 1,280-pixel-wide panel at that desktop size, yet the picker, numeric inputs, and balance were stacked. Keep Alloy Family as a focused selection screen. In Composition, put the element tiles on the left and a live composition bar and editable amounts on the right. In Create Alloy, `4 wt% Cu + 1 wt% Mg` should immediately show **95 wt% Al · Balance**. Optimize Alloy already computes the balance range. Give it the same visual prominence. In Processing, put the thermal sketch beside the temperature fields. Use readable field labels with units, and reveal longer help when it applies. The current Auto temperature explanation, for example, stays visible in Manual mode.

**Make element changes feel like they belong to the lattice.** Crossfade between family lattices in place. For an addition, I’d try a few edge atoms briefly splitting into paired glows, then settling. Keep that motion decorative and preserve the reduced-motion setting.

**Keep the JT startup animation.** I’d treat it as your maker’s signature and remove the persistent JoelTech footer. Put **Quit Rutile** in Settings and have it use the server’s existing shutdown cleanup. Closing a regular browser tab is an unreliable shutdown signal. If closing the window should always quit the app, have a desktop wrapper own the window and server process. [Chrome’s page lifecycle guidance](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/web-platform/page-lifecycle-api)

I checked the current UI in Edge at desktop and mobile widths and tested the automatic balance in the preview. The app code was left untouched.

import os
from pathlib import Path
import socket
import subprocess
import sys
import time

import requests
from playwright.sync_api import sync_playwright


def main():
    root = Path.cwd()
    output = root / 'workspace' / 'ui-critique' / 'desktop-revision'
    output.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    with socket.socket() as s:
        s.bind(('127.0.0.1', 0))
        port = s.getsockname()[1]
    base = f'http://127.0.0.1:{port}'
    env = dict(os.environ, RUTILE_WORKSPACE=str(output), RUTILE_CATALOG_PATH=str(output / 'catalog.sqlite3'), RUTILE_TEST_URL=base)
    with (output / 'server.log').open('w') as log:
        server = subprocess.Popen([sys.executable, 'scripts/run_app.py', '--port', str(port)], env=env, stdout=log, stderr=log, creationflags=subprocess.CREATE_NO_WINDOW)
        try:
            for _ in range(120):
                try:
                    if requests.get(base, timeout=1).ok:
                        break
                except requests.RequestException:
                    time.sleep(.25)
            else:
                raise AssertionError('Server startup timed out')

            with sync_playwright() as p:
                browser = p.chromium.launch(channel='msedge', headless=True)
                page = browser.new_page(viewport={'width': 1440, 'height': 810}, reduced_motion='reduce')
                errors = []
                page.on('pageerror', lambda error: errors.append(str(error)))
                page.goto(base)
                page.get_by_role('button', name='Start', exact=True).click()
                page.locator('#menu-optimize').click()
                page.locator('#studio-create').click()
                page.locator('#family-al').click()
                panel = page.locator('.optimizer-panel')
                for width,height in [(1440,810),(1920,1080),(1200,1920)]:
                    page.set_viewport_size({'width':width,'height':height})
                    family_width = panel.bounding_box()['width']
                    page.locator('#opt-next').click()
                    composition_width = panel.bounding_box()['width']
                    assert composition_width > family_width + 40, (width,family_width,composition_width)
                    assert page.evaluate('document.documentElement.scrollWidth <= innerWidth')
                    print(f'{width}x{height}: family {family_width:.0f}px → composition {composition_width:.0f}px')
                    if width==1440:
                        page.screenshot(path=output / 'composition.png', full_page=True)
                    page.locator('#opt-previous').click()

                for _ in range(2):
                    page.locator('#shell-back').click()
                page.locator('#menu-diagrams').click()
                for name in ('AlCu-21Kro','ReW'):
                    path = root / 'examples' / f'{name}.tdb'
                    if not path.exists():
                        continue
                    page.locator('#upload').set_input_files(path)
                    page.locator('#calculation-settings > summary').click()
                    page.locator('#temperature-mode').select_option('manual' if name.startswith('Al') else 'auto')
                    page.locator('#resolution').select_option('31,25')
                    page.locator('#calculation-settings > summary').click()
                    page.locator('#calculate').click()
                    page.wait_for_function("!document.querySelector('#export').disabled", timeout=180_000)
                    labels = page.locator('[data-region-label]')
                    print(name, labels.evaluate_all('nodes => nodes.map(e => [e.dataset.regionLabel,e.dataset.labelPlacement])'))
                    page.set_viewport_size({'width':1440,'height':810})
                    page.screenshot(path=output / f'{name}.png', full_page=True)
                    assert not errors, errors
                browser.close()
            subprocess.run([sys.executable, 'scripts/check_browser.py'], env=env, check=True)
        finally:
            server.terminate()
            server.wait(timeout=10)


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

RUTILE_TEST_URL selects the running server. --matcalc also checks the three
bundled family companions. Outputs stay in ignored workspace/.
"""
import argparse
import base64
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
from time import monotonic, sleep

import requests
from playwright.sync_api import expect, sync_playwright

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
BASE = os.environ.get("RUTILE_TEST_URL", "http://127.0.0.1:8000")


def submit(payload):
    # A completed result can be published just before its worker exits. Wait for
    # that worker to retire before submitting the next calculation on this test server.
    for _ in range(50):
        response = requests.post(f"{BASE}/api/processing", json=payload, timeout=30)
        if response.status_code == 422 and response.json().get("detail") == "A calculation is already running. Wait or cancel it first.":
            sleep(.1)
            continue
        break
    assert response.status_code == 202, response.text
    response.raise_for_status()
    job = response.json()["id"]
    deadline = monotonic() + 240
    while monotonic() < deadline:
        status = requests.get(f"{BASE}/api/jobs/{job}", timeout=30).json()

## Alloy studio

1. Open **Alloy studio → Create alloy** and select an aluminum, iron, or nickel
   family. Choose mass percent (wt%) or atomic percent (at%) and enter the amount
   of each element. The total must be 100%. **Use balance** fills the base amount.
2. In **Processing**, set the initial annealed equilibrium temperature, fully
   mixed melt temperature, final temperature, and pressure. The bundled MatCalc
   thermodynamic assessment and its matching mobility file load by default.
3. Open **Review your alloy setup** and select **Simulate phases**. Inspect the
   initial, melt, and cooled states, the cooling path, and tracer diffusivity
   where supported. **Export phase JSON** saves the result and source provenance.

**Optimize alloy** is not fully implemented. More attributes to be optimized for and a
full materials project api translation layer will be implemented first.

Rutile checks that the chosen melt temperature produces a fully liquid state and
samples equilibrium during cooling. The model assumes a homogeneous alloy, no
composition loss, and complete redistribution at each sampled temperature. This 
will be expanded upon later.
[Processing methods and limits](docs/processing.md)

For plain-carbon steel, choose **Iron**, select **Carbon** alone, and use the
default **Plain-carbon steel (Fe–Fe₃C)** phase selection in Processing. Try
0.40 wt% C in Create alloy and select **Use balance** before continuing.
[Steel phase selection and limits](docs/processing.md#plain-carbon-steel-equilibrium)

### Bundled databases
## Plain-carbon steel equilibrium

In Alloy Studio, choose **Iron** and select **Carbon** as the sole addition.
With the default MatCalc Fe 2.062 source, **Processing → Phase selection**
defaults to **Plain-carbon steel (Fe–Fe₃C)**. Try 0.40 wt% C in Create alloy
and use **Use balance** for Fe. Optimize alloy retains the half-maximum rule,
so a maximum of 0.80 wt% C gives the same nominal composition.

The steel policy considers liquid, ferrite, austenite and cementite at every
stage. It suspends graphite and specialized models such as `BCC_DISL` and
`H_BCC`. This is the conventional metastable Fe–Fe₃C equilibrium used for

content.text:
I updated Rutile around the desktop experience and kept the glass and glow.

- **Title screen** now says **Start**. Dragging and arrow keys still rotate the crystal, with the interaction left for people to discover.
- **Alloy Studio** widens after Alloy Family. Composition puts the glowing element tiles beside the amount editor. In Create Alloy, entering 4 wt% Cu and 1 wt% Mg automatically gives 95 wt% Al, shown in a live composition bar. [Composition screenshot](Y:/Rutile3/workspace/ui-critique/desktop-revision/composition.png)
- **Phase diagrams** have a shorter header so the plot and axes fit at 1440 × 810. Labels are smaller and borderless, with a dark halo for contrast. Narrow fields use short leaders to nearby labels. The right margin is available when a label can’t fit locally. Labels still support dragging, keyboard movement, and reset. [Al–Cu screenshot](Y:/Rutile3/workspace/ui-critique/desktop-revision/AlCu-21Kro-viewport.png)

I checked two 16:9 desktop sizes and a portrait desktop layout, ran Al–Cu and Re–W in Edge, and verified the automatic balance through processing and JSON export. All 109 backend tests passed.

import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import socket
import subprocess
import sys
import time

import requests
from playwright.sync_api import sync_playwright


def main():
    root = Path.cwd()
    output = root / 'workspace' / 'ui-critique' / 'desktop-revision'
    source = root / 'workspace' / 'ui-critique' / 'runs'
    with socket.socket() as sock:
        sock.bind(('127.0.0.1', 0))
        port = sock.getsockname()[1]
    base = f'http://127.0.0.1:{port}'
    env = dict(os.environ, RUTILE_WORKSPACE=str(output), RUTILE_CATALOG_PATH=str(output / 'catalog.sqlite3'), RUTILE_TEST_URL=base)
    with (output / 'inspector-server.log').open('w') as log:
        server = subprocess.Popen([sys.executable, 'scripts/run_app.py', '--port', str(port)], env=env, stdout=log, stderr=log, creationflags=subprocess.CREATE_NO_WINDOW)
        try:
            for _ in range(120):
                try:
                    if requests.get(base, timeout=1).ok:
                        break
                except requests.RequestException:
                    time.sleep(.25)
            else:
                raise AssertionError('Server startup timed out')
            subprocess.run([sys.executable, 'scripts/check_plot_ui.py'], env=env, check=True)
            result = json.loads(next(source.glob('*/result.json')).read_text())
            with sync_playwright() as p:
                browser = p.chromium.launch(channel='msedge', headless=True)
                page = browser.new_page(viewport={'width':1440, 'height':810}, reduced_motion='reduce')
                page.route('**/api/diagrams', lambda route: route.fulfill(json={'id':'saved-alcu'}))
                page.route('**/api/jobs/saved-alcu', lambda route: route.fulfill(json={'state':'completed'}))
                page.route('**/api/jobs/saved-alcu/result', lambda route: route.fulfill(json=result))
                page.goto(base)
                page.get_by_role('button',name='Start',exact=True).click()
                page.locator('#menu-diagrams').click()
                page.locator('#upload').set_input_files(root / 'examples' / 'AlCu-21Kro.tdb')
                page.locator('#calculate').click()
                page.wait_for_function("document.querySelector('#workspace').dataset.stage==='complete'")
                point = page.evaluate("""() => {
                    const plot = document.querySelector('#plot'), p = plot.createSVGPoint();
                    p.x = 76 + .10 * 670; p.y = 25 + .50 * 465;
                    const q = p.matrixTransform(plot.getScreenCTM()); return [q.x,q.y];
                }""")
                page.mouse.click(*point)
                page.mouse.move(8, 8)
                assert page.locator('#point-structure').inner_text() == 'FCC + C16'
                assert page.locator('#legend').is_hidden()
                assert page.locator('#point-audit-content').is_hidden()
                assert page.locator('#diagram-details').bounding_box()['y'] > page.locator('.setup').bounding_box()['y']
                assert page.locator('#phase-key').bounding_box()['y'] > page.locator('.inspector-panel').bounding_box()['y']
                page.screenshot(path=output / 'phase-inspector.png')
                page.locator('#point-audit-title').click()
                assert page.get_by_text('Nearest sample', exact=False).is_visible()
                page.locator('#phase-key summary').click()
                assert page.locator('#legend').is_visible()
                assert page.evaluate("document.documentElement.scrollWidth === innerWidth")
                print('PASS desktop phase inspector layout and disclosures with a saved Al-Cu result')
        finally:
            server.terminate()
            server.wait(timeout=10)


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

"""Bounded liquidus preflight for automatic binary diagram temperature ranges."""
import math

import numpy as np
from pycalphad import Model, equilibrium, variables as v

from rutile3.engines.tdb import available_phases, parse_tdb, solver_models

SAMPLE_COUNT = 10
PADDING_K = 30.
BRACKET_TOLERANCE_K = .25
MAX_TEMPERATURE_K = 6000.


def search_liquidus(evaluate, lower, ceiling, progress=lambda value: None):
    """Bracket/refine last-solid disappearance at ten fixed mole fractions.

    evaluate(T, indices) returns fully-liquid flags, raising on unresolved states.
    Normal melting (solid disappears on heating) is assumed. Bounded discovery
    cannot rule out narrow peaks between composition probes or reentrant phases.
    """
    if ceiling < lower:
        raise ValueError("Auto temperature has no search interval within the documented limits. Use Manual.")
    last_solid = [None]*SAMPLE_COUNT
    upper = [None]*SAMPLE_COUNT
    pending = list(range(SAMPLE_COUNT))
    temperature = lower
    evaluations = 0
    while pending:
        states = evaluate(temperature, pending)
        evaluations += len(pending)
        for index, liquid in zip(pending, states, strict=True):
            if liquid:
                upper[index] = temperature
            else:
                last_solid[index] = temperature
        pending = [i for i in pending if upper[i] is None]
        progress({"stage": "temperature", "percent": 100*(SAMPLE_COUNT-len(pending))/21,
                  "completed_steps": SAMPLE_COUNT-len(pending), "total_steps": 21, "step_unit": "probe steps",
                  "message": f"Finding melting range · {SAMPLE_COUNT-len(pending)} of {SAMPLE_COUNT} compositions bracketed at {temperature:.1f} K"})
        if pending and temperature >= ceiling:
            raise ValueError(f"Auto temperature could not find a fully liquid state at {len(pending)} of 10 compositions "
                             f"below {ceiling:g} K. Use Manual or a database with suitable liquid coverage.")
        temperature = min(ceiling, max(temperature+100., temperature*1.35))
    probes = []
    for index in range(SAMPLE_COUNT):
        low, high = last_solid[index], upper[index]
        already_liquid = low is None
        if not already_liquid:
            while high-low > BRACKET_TOLERANCE_K:
                middle = (low+high)/2
                liquid, = evaluate(middle, [index])
                evaluations += 1
                if liquid:
                    high = middle
                else:
                    low = middle
        upper[index] = high
        probes.append({"overall_mole_fraction_b": index/(SAMPLE_COUNT-1),
                       "solver_mole_fraction_b": float(np.clip(index/(SAMPLE_COUNT-1), 1e-6, 1-1e-6)),
                       "liquidus_bracket_k": None if already_liquid else [low, high],
                       "fully_liquid_at_k": high,
                       "status": "already_liquid_at_lower_bound" if already_liquid else "bracketed"})
        progress({"stage": "temperature", "percent": 100*(SAMPLE_COUNT+index+1)/21,
                  "completed_steps": SAMPLE_COUNT+index+1, "total_steps": 21, "step_unit": "probe steps",
                  "message": f"Refining melting estimate · composition {index+1} of 10"})
    # Use upper bracket edges so solver uncertainty never consumes the 30 K margin.
    maximum = max(upper)
    top = min(float(math.ceil(maximum+PADDING_K)), ceiling+PADDING_K)
    if not all(evaluate(top, list(range(SAMPLE_COUNT)))):
        raise ValueError("Auto temperature could not confirm liquid across the composition probes at the padded limit. Use Manual.")
    evaluations += SAMPLE_COUNT
    progress({"stage": "temperature", "percent": 100, "completed_steps": 21, "total_steps": 21,
              "step_unit": "probe steps", "message": "Melting range confirmed across all 10 probes"})
    return {"temperature_min": lower, "temperature_max": top,
            "sample_count": SAMPLE_COUNT, "padding_k": PADDING_K,
            "maximum_liquidus_upper_bound_k": maximum,
            "bracket_tolerance_k": BRACKET_TOLERANCE_K, "search_ceiling_k": ceiling,
            "equilibria_evaluated": evaluations, "probes": probes,
            "method": "Ten composition probes; bounded heating search and bisection to fully liquid equilibrium",
            "assumptions": ["Normal melting on heating; fully liquid means no solid molar fraction above 1e-6.",
                            "Near-pure endpoints use 1e-6 and 1-1e-6 mole fraction for solver stability.",
                            "Ten composition probes may miss a liquidus maximum between probes; not a certified global maximum.",
                            "Already-liquid probes bound melting at or below the lower graph limit; they do not measure a melting temperature."]}


def estimate_temperature_range(raw, settings, progress, documented_limits=None):
    db = parse_tdb(raw)
    phases, components = available_phases(db, settings["components"])
    if "LIQUID" not in phases:
        raise ValueError("Auto temperature requires a compatible LIQUID phase with Gibbs-energy data. Choose Manual for this database.")
    lower = max(300., documented_limits[0]) if documented_limits else 300.
    limit = min(MAX_TEMPERATURE_K, documented_limits[1]) if documented_limits else MAX_TEMPERATURE_K
    models, excluded = solver_models(db, components, phases)
    phases = sorted(models)
    xs = np.clip(np.linspace(0, 1, SAMPLE_COUNT), 1e-6, 1-1e-6)
    def evaluate(temperature, indices):
        try:
            eq = equilibrium(db, components, phases,
                             {v.N: 1, v.P: settings["pressure"], v.T: float(temperature),
                              v.X(settings["components"][1]): xs[indices]},
                             model=models, calc_opts={"pdens": 1000})
            states = []
            order = [str(c) for c in eq.component.values]
            component_index = order.index(settings["components"][1])
            for position, index in enumerate(indices):
                point = eq.isel({"X_"+settings["components"][1]: position})
                names, amounts = point.Phase.values.reshape(-1), point.NP.values.reshape(-1)
                active = (names != "") & np.isfinite(amounts) & (amounts > 1e-9)
                names, amounts = names[active], amounts[active]
                compositions = point.X.values.reshape(-1, len(order))[active, component_index]
                if not math.isfinite(float(point.GM.values.item())) or not len(names) or not np.all(np.isfinite(compositions)) or \
                        abs(float(sum(amounts))-1) > 1e-4 or abs(float(sum(amounts*compositions))-xs[index]) > 1e-4:
                    raise ValueError("unresolved equilibrium or failed mass balance")
                non_liquid = sum(float(f) for p, f in zip(names, amounts) if p != "LIQUID")
                liquid = sum(float(f) for p, f in zip(names, amounts) if p == "LIQUID")
                states.append(non_liquid <= 1e-6 and liquid >= 1-1e-6)
            return states
        except Exception as exc:
            raise ValueError(f"Auto temperature could not resolve equilibrium at {temperature:.2f} K: {exc}. Choose Manual.") from exc
    result = search_liquidus(evaluate, lower, limit-PADDING_K, progress)
    result["documented_temperature_limits_k"] = documented_limits
    result["equivalent_phase_exclusions"] = excluded
    return result
"""Automatic ranges: bounded search and an analytical ideal binary liquidus."""
import json
import math

import pytest
from scipy.optimize import brentq

from rutile3.domain.diagrams import DiagramRequest
from rutile3.engines.temperature import estimate_temperature_range, search_liquidus
import rutile3.jobs.worker as worker

# Synthetic ideal solutions with pure-element melting at 1,000 and 2,000 K.
# Equality of chemical potentials gives the analytical liquidus used below.
IDEAL_MELTING = b"""
ELEMENT AL FCC_A1 26.9815 0 0 !
ELEMENT CU FCC_A1 63.546 0 0 !
TYPE_DEFINITION % SEQ * !
PHASE FCC_A1 % 1 1 !
CONSTITUENT FCC_A1 :AL,CU: !
PARAMETER G(FCC_A1,AL;0) 1 0; 6000 N !
PARAMETER G(FCC_A1,CU;0) 1 0; 6000 N !
PHASE LIQUID % 1 1 !
CONSTITUENT LIQUID :AL,CU: !
PARAMETER G(LIQUID,AL;0) 1 10000-10*T; 6000 N !
PARAMETER G(LIQUID,CU;0) 1 20000-10*T; 6000 N !
"""


def test_auto_range_matches_analytical_ideal_liquidus():
    result = estimate_temperature_range(IDEAL_MELTING, {"components": ["AL", "CU"], "pressure": 101325}, lambda v: None)
    assert result["temperature_min"] == 300
    assert len(result["probes"]) == 10
    for probe in result["probes"]:
        x = probe["solver_mole_fraction_b"]
        expected = brentq(lambda t: (1-x)*math.exp((10000-10*t)/(8.3145*t)) +
                                   x*math.exp((20000-10*t)/(8.3145*t))-1, 500, 3000)
        low, high = probe["liquidus_bracket_k"]
        assert high-low <= .25
        assert high == pytest.approx(expected, abs=.3)  # 0.25 K bracket + vanishing-solid threshold.
    assert 2030 <= result["temperature_max"] <= 2031
    assert result["temperature_max"] >= result["maximum_liquidus_upper_bound_k"]+30
    json.dumps(result, allow_nan=False)


def test_bounded_search_uses_hottest_probe_and_confirms_padded_limit():
    melts = [900, 1000, 1200, 1400, 1600, 1800, 1700, 1500, 1300, 1100]
    calls = []
    def evaluate(t, indices):
        calls.append((t, indices))
        return [t >= melts[i] for i in indices]
    updates = []
    result = search_liquidus(evaluate, 300, 5970, updates.append)
    assert 1830 <= result["temperature_max"] <= 1831
    assert calls[-1] == (result["temperature_max"], list(range(10)))
    assert all(t <= 6000 for t, _ in calls)
    assert updates[-1]["completed_steps"] == updates[-1]["total_steps"] == 21
    assert [p["completed_steps"] for p in updates] == sorted(p["completed_steps"] for p in updates)


def test_already_liquid_probes_do_not_invent_melting_temperatures():
    result = search_liquidus(lambda t, indices: [True]*len(indices), 300, 5970)
    assert result["temperature_max"] == 330
    assert all(p["liquidus_bracket_k"] is None and p["status"] == "already_liquid_at_lower_bound"
               for p in result["probes"])


def test_unmelted_or_missing_liquid_and_documented_limits_fail_explicitly():
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="could not find a fully liquid"):
        search_liquidus(lambda t, indices: [False]*len(indices), 300, 5970)
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="LIQUID phase"):
        estimate_temperature_range(IDEAL_MELTING.replace(b"LIQUID", b"BCC_A2"),
                                   {"components": ["AL", "CU"], "pressure": 101325}, lambda v: None)
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="could not find a fully liquid"):
        estimate_temperature_range(IDEAL_MELTING, {"components": ["AL", "CU"], "pressure": 101325},
                                   lambda v: None, documented_limits=[1, 2010])


def test_margin_requires_fully_liquid_confirmation():
    def evaluate(t, indices):
        return [1000 <= t < 1020]*len(indices)
    # Liquid at the initial floor is insufficient if it is no longer liquid at
    # the padded graph limit: a reentrant solid must fail confirmation.
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="padded limit"):
        search_liquidus(evaluate, 1000, 5970)


def test_auto_request_does_not_validate_unused_manual_order():
    request = DiagramRequest(components=["AL", "CU"], temperature_mode="auto",
                             temperature_min=1200, temperature_max=300)
    assert request.temperature_mode == "auto"


def test_worker_persists_resolved_settings_and_original_request(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    source = tmp_path / "source.tdb"
    source.write_bytes(IDEAL_MELTING)
    settings = {"temperature_mode": "auto", "temperature_min": 300, "temperature_max": 1200,
                "temperature_points": 11, "components": ["AL", "CU"], "pressure": 101325}
    (tmp_path / "request.json").write_text(json.dumps({"database_path": str(source), "settings": settings}))
    estimate = {"temperature_min": 300, "temperature_max": 2031, "sample_count": 10}
    monkeypatch.setattr(worker, "estimate_temperature_range", lambda *a: estimate)
    def calculate(path, resolved, progress, raw):
        assert resolved["temperature_max"] == 2031
        progress({"stage": "mapping"})
        return {"settings": resolved, "provenance": {}}
    monkeypatch.setattr(worker, "calculate_binary", calculate)
    worker.run(tmp_path)
    result = json.loads((tmp_path / "result.json").read_text())
    assert result["settings"]["temperature_max"] == 2031
    assert result["provenance"]["temperature_range_estimate"] == estimate
    preview = json.loads((tmp_path / "preview.json").read_text())
    assert preview["settings"]["temperature_max"] == 2031

The validation lattice never supplies boundary positions. A missing map prediction

def base_phase(label):
    return label.split("#")[0].strip()


def serialize_map(strategy, component):
    ribbons, invariants = [], []
    for region in strategy.get_tieline_data(v.X(component), v.T):
        if len(region.data) != 2:
            continue
        a, b = region.data
        ties, chunks = [], []
        for xa, ta, xb, tb in zip(a.x, a.y, b.x, b.y):
            if not all(np.isfinite(z) for z in (xa, ta, xb, tb)) or abs(ta-tb) > 1e-3:
                if len(ties) > 1:
                    chunks.append(ties)
                ties = []
                continue
            ends = sorted([(float(xa), base_phase(a.phase)), (float(xb), base_phase(b.phase))])
            if ends[1][0] - ends[0][0] < 1e-10:
                continue
            ties.append({"temperature": float(ta), "left": ends[0][0], "right": ends[1][0],
                         "phases": [ends[0][1], ends[1][1]]})
        if len(ties) > 1:
            chunks.append(ties)
        ribbons.extend({"ties": chunk} for chunk in chunks)
    for region in strategy.get_invariant_data(v.X(component), v.T):
        points = sorted((float(np.asarray(p.x).item()), float(np.asarray(p.y).item()), base_phase(p.phase))
                        for p in region.data)
        if all(math.isfinite(z) for p in points for z in p[:2]):
            invariants.append({"temperature": points[0][1],
                               "compositions": [p[0] for p in points], "phases": [p[2] for p in points]})
    return {"ribbons": ribbons, "invariants": invariants}

def lower_energy_hull(xs, energies):
    """Indices of the lower convex envelope of sampled binary molar energies."""
    finite = np.flatnonzero(np.isfinite(xs) & np.isfinite(energies))
    order = finite[np.lexsort((energies[finite], xs[finite]))]
    hull = []
    # Python floats avoid millions of NumPy scalar operations in this small
    # sequential stack algorithm; sorting/filtering remain vectorized.
    for c, x, energy in zip(order.tolist(), xs[order].tolist(), energies[order].tolist()):
        if hull and x == hull[-1][1]:
            continue  # Lowest energy at this exact composition sorts first.
        while len(hull) >= 2:
            a, b = hull[-2:]
            cross = (b[1]-a[1])*(energy-a[2]) - (b[2]-a[2])*(x-a[1])
            if cross > 0:

            hull.pop()
        hull.append((c, x, energy))
    return [p[0] for p in hull]

"""Bounded liquidus preflight for automatic binary diagram temperature ranges."""
import math

import numpy as np
from pycalphad import Model, equilibrium, variables as v

from rutile3.engines.tdb import available_phases, parse_tdb, solver_models

SAMPLE_COUNT = 10
PADDING_K = 30.
BRACKET_TOLERANCE_K = .25
MAX_TEMPERATURE_K = 6000.


def search_liquidus(evaluate, lower, ceiling, progress=lambda value: None):
    """Bracket/refine last-solid disappearance at ten fixed mole fractions.

    evaluate(T, indices) returns fully-liquid flags, raising on unresolved states.
    Normal melting (solid disappears on heating) is assumed. Bounded discovery
    cannot rule out narrow peaks between composition probes or reentrant phases.
    """
    if ceiling < lower:
        raise ValueError("Auto temperature has no search interval within the documented limits. Use Manual.")
    last_solid = [None]*SAMPLE_COUNT
    upper = [None]*SAMPLE_COUNT
    pending = list(range(SAMPLE_COUNT))
    temperature = lower
    evaluations = 0
    while pending:
        states = evaluate(temperature, pending)
        evaluations += len(pending)
        for index, liquid in zip(pending, states, strict=True):
            if liquid:
                upper[index] = temperature
            else:
                last_solid[index] = temperature
        pending = [i for i in pending if upper[i] is None]
        progress({"stage": "temperature", "percent": 100*(SAMPLE_COUNT-len(pending))/21,
                  "completed_steps": SAMPLE_COUNT-len(pending), "total_steps": 21, "step_unit": "probe steps",
                  "message": f"Finding melting range · {SAMPLE_COUNT-len(pending)} of {SAMPLE_COUNT} compositions bracketed at {temperature:.1f} K"})
        if pending and temperature >= ceiling:
            raise ValueError(f"Auto temperature could not find a fully liquid state at {len(pending)} of 10 compositions "
                             f"below {ceiling:g} K. Use Manual or a database with suitable liquid coverage.")
        temperature = min(ceiling, max(temperature+100., temperature*1.35))
    probes = []
    for index in range(SAMPLE_COUNT):
        low, high = last_solid[index], upper[index]
        already_liquid = low is None
        if not already_liquid:
            while high-low > BRACKET_TOLERANCE_K:
                middle = (low+high)/2
                liquid, = evaluate(middle, [index])
                evaluations += 1
                if liquid:
                    high = middle
                else:
                    low = middle
        upper[index] = high
        probes.append({"overall_mole_fraction_b": index/(SAMPLE_COUNT-1),
                       "solver_mole_fraction_b": float(np.clip(index/(SAMPLE_COUNT-1), 1e-6, 1-1e-6)),
                       "liquidus_bracket_k": None if already_liquid else [low, high],
                       "fully_liquid_at_k": high,
                       "status": "already_liquid_at_lower_bound" if already_liquid else "bracketed"})
        progress({"stage": "temperature", "percent": 100*(SAMPLE_COUNT+index+1)/21,
                  "completed_steps": SAMPLE_COUNT+index+1, "total_steps": 21, "step_unit": "probe steps",
                  "message": f"Refining melting estimate · composition {index+1} of 10"})
    # Use upper bracket edges so solver uncertainty never consumes the 30 K margin.
    maximum = max(upper)
    top = min(float(math.ceil(maximum+PADDING_K)), ceiling+PADDING_K)
    if not all(evaluate(top, list(range(SAMPLE_COUNT)))):
        raise ValueError("Auto temperature could not confirm liquid across the composition probes at the padded limit. Use Manual.")
    evaluations += SAMPLE_COUNT
    progress({"stage": "temperature", "percent": 100, "completed_steps": 21, "total_steps": 21,
              "step_unit": "probe steps", "message": "Melting range confirmed across all 10 probes"})
    return {"temperature_min": lower, "temperature_max": top,
            "sample_count": SAMPLE_COUNT, "padding_k": PADDING_K,
            "maximum_liquidus_upper_bound_k": maximum,
            "bracket_tolerance_k": BRACKET_TOLERANCE_K, "search_ceiling_k": ceiling,
            "equilibria_evaluated": evaluations, "probes": probes,
            "method": "Ten composition probes; bounded heating search and bisection to fully liquid equilibrium",
            "assumptions": ["Normal melting on heating; fully liquid means no solid molar fraction above 1e-6.",
                            "Near-pure endpoints use 1e-6 and 1-1e-6 mole fraction for solver stability.",
                            "Ten composition probes may miss a liquidus maximum between probes; not a certified global maximum.",
                            "Already-liquid probes bound melting at or below the lower graph limit; they do not measure a melting temperature."]}


def estimate_temperature_range(raw, settings, progress, documented_limits=None):
    db = parse_tdb(raw)
    phases, components = available_phases(db, settings["components"])
    if "LIQUID" not in phases:
        raise ValueError("Auto temperature requires a compatible LIQUID phase with Gibbs-energy data. Choose Manual for this database.")
    lower = max(300., documented_limits[0]) if documented_limits else 300.
    limit = min(MAX_TEMPERATURE_K, documented_limits[1]) if documented_limits else MAX_TEMPERATURE_K
    models, excluded = solver_models(db, components, phases)
    phases = sorted(models)
    xs = np.clip(np.linspace(0, 1, SAMPLE_COUNT), 1e-6, 1-1e-6)
    def evaluate(temperature, indices):
        try:
            eq = equilibrium(db, components, phases,
                             {v.N: 1, v.P: settings["pressure"], v.T: float(temperature),
                              v.X(settings["components"][1]): xs[indices]},
                             model=models, calc_opts={"pdens": 1000})
            states = []
            order = [str(c) for c in eq.component.values]
            component_index = order.index(settings["components"][1])
            for position, index in enumerate(indices):
                point = eq.isel({"X_"+settings["components"][1]: position})
                names, amounts = point.Phase.values.reshape(-1), point.NP.values.reshape(-1)
                active = (names != "") & np.isfinite(amounts) & (amounts > 1e-9)
                names, amounts = names[active], amounts[active]
                compositions = point.X.values.reshape(-1, len(order))[active, component_index]
                if not math.isfinite(float(point.GM.values.item())) or not len(names) or not np.all(np.isfinite(compositions)) or \
                        abs(float(sum(amounts))-1) > 1e-4 or abs(float(sum(amounts*compositions))-xs[index]) > 1e-4:
                    raise ValueError("unresolved equilibrium or failed mass balance")
                non_liquid = sum(float(f) for p, f in zip(names, amounts) if p != "LIQUID")
                liquid = sum(float(f) for p, f in zip(names, amounts) if p == "LIQUID")
                states.append(non_liquid <= 1e-6 and liquid >= 1-1e-6)
            return states
        except Exception as exc:
            raise ValueError(f"Auto temperature could not resolve equilibrium at {temperature:.2f} K: {exc}. Choose Manual.") from exc
    result = search_liquidus(evaluate, lower, limit-PADDING_K, progress)
    result["documented_temperature_limits_k"] = documented_limits
    result["equivalent_phase_exclusions"] = excluded
    return result

# Synthetic ideal solutions with pure-element melting at 1,000 and 2,000 K.
# Equality of chemical potentials gives the analytical liquidus used below.
IDEAL_MELTING = b"""
ELEMENT AL FCC_A1 26.9815 0 0 !
ELEMENT CU FCC_A1 63.546 0 0 !
TYPE_DEFINITION % SEQ * !
PHASE FCC_A1 % 1 1 !
CONSTITUENT FCC_A1 :AL,CU: !
PARAMETER G(FCC_A1,AL;0) 1 0; 6000 N !
PARAMETER G(FCC_A1,CU;0) 1 0; 6000 N !
PHASE LIQUID % 1 1 !
CONSTITUENT LIQUID :AL,CU: !
PARAMETER G(LIQUID,AL;0) 1 10000-10*T; 6000 N !
PARAMETER G(LIQUID,CU;0) 1 20000-10*T; 6000 N !
"""


def test_auto_range_matches_analytical_ideal_liquidus():
    result = estimate_temperature_range(IDEAL_MELTING, {"components": ["AL", "CU"], "pressure": 101325}, lambda v: None)
    assert result["temperature_min"] == 300
    assert len(result["probes"]) == 10
    for probe in result["probes"]:
        x = probe["solver_mole_fraction_b"]
        expected = brentq(lambda t: (1-x)*math.exp((10000-10*t)/(8.3145*t)) +
                                   x*math.exp((20000-10*t)/(8.3145*t))-1, 500, 3000)
        low, high = probe["liquidus_bracket_k"]
        assert high-low <= .25
        assert high == pytest.approx(expected, abs=.3)  # 0.25 K bracket + vanishing-solid threshold.
    assert 2030 <= result["temperature_max"] <= 2031
    assert result["temperature_max"] >= result["maximum_liquidus_upper_bound_k"]+30
    json.dumps(result, allow_nan=False)

"""Binary boundary mapping and tie-line interpolation, independent of HTTP/plotting.

The validation lattice never supplies boundary positions. A missing map prediction
is explicitly unverified; interpolated tie lines are not fresh equilibria.
"""
from collections import Counter
from itertools import combinations
import math
from time import monotonic

import numpy as np
from pycalphad import Model, calculate, equilibrium, variables as v
from pycalphad.codegen.phase_record_factory import PhaseRecordFactory
from pycalphad.mapping import BinaryStrategy


def base_phase(label):
    return label.split("#")[0].strip()


def serialize_map(strategy, component):
    ribbons, invariants = [], []
    for region in strategy.get_tieline_data(v.X(component), v.T):
        if len(region.data) != 2:
            continue
        a, b = region.data
        ties, chunks = [], []
        for xa, ta, xb, tb in zip(a.x, a.y, b.x, b.y):
            if not all(np.isfinite(z) for z in (xa, ta, xb, tb)) or abs(ta-tb) > 1e-3:
                if len(ties) > 1:
                    chunks.append(ties)
                ties = []
                continue
            ends = sorted([(float(xa), base_phase(a.phase)), (float(xb), base_phase(b.phase))])
            if ends[1][0] - ends[0][0] < 1e-10:
                continue
            ties.append({"temperature": float(ta), "left": ends[0][0], "right": ends[1][0],
                         "phases": [ends[0][1], ends[1][1]]})
        if len(ties) > 1:
            chunks.append(ties)
        ribbons.extend({"ties": chunk} for chunk in chunks)
    for region in strategy.get_invariant_data(v.X(component), v.T):
        points = sorted((float(np.asarray(p.x).item()), float(np.asarray(p.y).item()), base_phase(p.phase))
                        for p in region.data)
        if all(math.isfinite(z) for p in points for z in p[:2]):
            invariants.append({"temperature": points[0][1],
                               "compositions": [p[0] for p in points], "phases": [p[2] for p in points]})
    return {"ribbons": ribbons, "invariants": invariants}


class ReportingBinaryStrategy(BinaryStrategy):
    """Report the four completed edge searches without copying the library loop."""
    def add_starting_points_from_step(self, step):
        super().add_starting_points_from_step(step)
        self.completed_edges += 1
        self.report_progress({"stage": "seeding", "completed_steps": self.completed_edges,
                              "total_steps": 4, "step_unit": "edges", "percent": 25*self.completed_edges,
                              "message": f"Finding starting equilibria · {self.completed_edges} of 4 edges"})


def trace_boundaries(db, components, phases, settings, progress):
    low, high = settings["temperature_min"], settings["temperature_max"]
    steps = settings.get("boundary_steps", 320)
    strategy = ReportingBinaryStrategy(db, components, phases,
                              {v.N: 1, v.P: settings["pressure"], v.T: (low, high, (high-low)/steps),
                               v.X(settings["components"][1]): (0, 1, 1/steps)},
                              GLOBAL_MIN_PDENS=1000)
    strategy.completed_edges, strategy.report_progress = 0, progress
    progress({"stage": "seeding", "message": "Finding starting equilibria along the diagram edges",
              "percent": 0, "completed_steps": 0, "total_steps": 4, "step_unit": "edges", "boundary_points": 0})
    strategy.generate_automatic_starting_points()
    last_update = 0
    for iteration in range(100000):
        finished = strategy.iterate()
        now = monotonic()
        if finished or now-last_update > 0.8:
            mapped = serialize_map(strategy, settings["components"][1])
            count = sum(len(r["ties"])*2 for r in mapped["ribbons"])
            progress({"stage": "mapping", "message": "Following phase boundaries and checking global stability",
                      "percent": None, "boundary_points": count, "iterations": iteration+1,
                      "completed_steps": None, "total_steps": None,
                      "preview": mapped})
            last_update = now
        if finished:
            failed = sum(line.status.name == "FAILED" for line in strategy.zpf_lines)
            mapped["failed_lines"] = failed
            if failed:
                mapped["notes"] = [f"{failed} boundary traces ended prematurely; inspect check disagreements and unverified coverage."]
            return mapped, strategy
    raise RuntimeError("Boundary tracing reached its iteration limit; the map is incomplete.")


def lower_energy_hull(xs, energies):
    """Indices of the lower convex envelope of sampled binary molar energies."""
    finite = np.flatnonzero(np.isfinite(xs) & np.isfinite(energies))
    order = finite[np.lexsort((energies[finite], xs[finite]))]
    hull = []
    # Python floats avoid millions of NumPy scalar operations in this small
    # sequential stack algorithm; sorting/filtering remain vectorized.
    for c, x, energy in zip(order.tolist(), xs[order].tolist(), energies[order].tolist()):
        if hull and x == hull[-1][1]:
            continue  # Lowest energy at this exact composition sorts first.
        while len(hull) >= 2:
            a, b = hull[-2:]
            cross = (b[1]-a[1])*(energy-a[2]) - (b[2]-a[2])*(x-a[1])
            if cross > 0:
                break
            hull.pop()
        hull.append((c, x, energy))
    return [p[0] for p in hull]

Bases: `object`

Base strategy class for phase diagram construction.

### Derived Classes¶

  * SteppingStrategy: For single-axis diagrams.

  * BinaryStrategy: For binary phase diagrams (1 composition, 1 potential axis).

  * TernaryStrategy: For ternary phase diagrams (2 composition axes).

  * IsoplethStrategy: For isopleths (tested only for 1 composition, 1 potential axis so far).

### Constants¶

DELTA_SCALE float
    

Factor to scale down step size if a single step iteration was unsuccessful (default: 0.5).

MIN_DELTA_RATIO float
    

Minimum step size (as ratio of default) before stopping ZPF line iteration (default: 0.1).

GLOBAL_CHECK_INTERVAL int
    

Number of iterations before global minimum check. Proceed with caution for any interval >1 (default: 1).

GLOBAL_MIN_PDENS int
    

Sampling density for global minimum check (default: 500).

GLOBAL_MIN_TOL float
    

Minimum driving force for a composition set to pass the global minimum check (default: 1e-4).

GLOBAL_MIN_NUM_CANDIDATES int
    

Number of candidates to search through for finding the global minimum. Sometimes, the global minimum can be missed if the sampling is poor, so checking the n-best candidates can help (default: 1000). (NOTE: this is not actually how many candidates the global eq check will solve the driving force. This value represents the N number of samples with the lowest sampled driving forces, then the driving force is computed for all unique phases from the candidates (which in large databases, this might be as high as 10-20), So increasing it to a high value does not significantly degrade performance and mapping using models with high DOF may be better)

"""TDB parsing and pycalphad model inspection."""
from pycalphad import Database, Model, variables as v
from pycalphad.core.utils import filter_phases


def parse_tdb(raw):
    try:
        content = raw.decode("utf-8-sig")
    except UnicodeDecodeError:
        content = raw.decode("cp1252")
    return Database(content.replace("\r\n", "\n").replace("\r", "\n"))


def available_phases(db, components):
    comps = list(components) + (["VA"] if "VA" in db.elements else [])
    phases = sorted(filter_phases(db, comps))
    energetic = {p["phase_name"] for p in db._parameters.all() if p["parameter_type"] == "G"}
    return [p for p in phases if p in energetic], comps


def solver_models(db, components, phases):
    """Remove only exact copies of a linked model's disordered contribution.

    A partitioned ordered model already includes its disordered state. Some
    assessments additionally define an identical standalone phase. Letting both
    compete creates degenerate phase identities. Never infer equivalence by name
    or sampled energy: require matching constitutions and symbolic GM equality.
    """
    models = {p: Model(db, components, p) for p in phases}
    excluded = []
    for ordered in phases:
        hints = db.phases[ordered].model_hints
        base = hints.get("disordered_phase")
        if not base or hints.get("ordered_phase") != ordered or base == ordered:
            continue
        reference = Model(db, components, base)
        for name in list(models):
            if name == ordered or db.phases[name].model_hints.get("ordered_phase"):
                continue
            candidate = models[name]
            if candidate.constituents != reference.constituents or candidate.site_ratios != reference.site_ratios:
                continue
            rename = {sf: v.SiteFraction(base, sf.sublattice_index, sf.species)
                      for sf in candidate.site_fractions}
            if candidate.GM.xreplace(rename) == reference.GM:
                excluded.append({"phase": name, "represented_by": ordered, "disordered_model": base,
                                 "reason": "Exact symbolic duplicate of the linked disordered Gibbs-energy model"})
                del models[name]
    return models, excluded


def describe(raw):
    db = parse_tdb(raw)
    types, interactions = set(), {}
    for parameter in db._parameters.all():
        family = parameter["parameter_type"]
        types.add(family)
        elements = sorted({element for sublattice in parameter["constituent_array"]
                           for species in sublattice for element in species.constituents
                           if element in db.elements and element not in {"VA", "/-"}})
        if len(elements) > 1:
            by_family = interactions.setdefault("-".join(elements), {})
            by_family.setdefault(family, set()).add(parameter["phase_name"])
    if not db.elements:
        raise ValueError("No elements were parsed.")
    families = {
        "thermodynamic": {"G"},
        "mobility": {"MQ", "MF", "DQ", "DF"},
        "volume": {"V0", "VA", "VK", "VC", "VS"},
    }
    return {
        "elements": sorted(db.elements - {"VA", "/-"}),
        "phases": sorted(db.phases),
        "phase_models": {name: {"site_ratios": list(phase.sublattices),
                                "constituents": [sorted(s.name for s in sub) for sub in phase.constituents],
                                "hints": phase.model_hints}
                         for name, phase in db.phases.items()},
        "parameter_types": sorted(types),
        "detected_interactions": {system: {family: sorted(phases) for family, phases in families.items()}
                                  for system, families in interactions.items()},
        "capabilities": [name for name, parameters in families.items() if parameters.intersection(types)],
        "has_gibbs_energy": "G" in types,
    }


def check_models(raw, components):
    phases, active = available_phases(db := parse_tdb(raw), components)
    if not phases:
        raise ValueError("No compatible phases with Gibbs-energy data are available.")
    for phase in phases:
        Model(db, active, phase)
    return phases
    """Discover tie-line seeds from one energy hull per T, then solve equilibrium.

    The hull is only a candidate generator. Returned coexistence compositions
    always come from converged pycalphad equilibria, never from sampled vertices.
    """
    records = records or PhaseRecordFactory(db, components, [v.N, v.P, v.T], models)
    ties, failures = [], []
    retried, seed_count, narrow_count = 0, 0, 0
    for t in group:
        grid = calculate(db, components, phases, T=float(t), P=settings["pressure"], N=1,
                         model=models, phase_records=records, output="GM", pdens=1000)
        xs = grid.X.sel(component=settings["components"][1]).values.reshape(-1)
        energies, names = grid.GM.values.reshape(-1), grid.Phase.values.reshape(-1)
        hull = lower_energy_hull(xs, energies)
        seeds, narrow = hull_probe_compositions(xs, names, hull, settings.get("boundary_steps", 320))
        seed_count += len(seeds)
        narrow_count += narrow
        if not seeds:
            continue
        eq = equilibrium(db, components, phases,
                         {v.N: 1, v.P: settings["pressure"], v.T: float(t),
                          v.X(settings["components"][1]): seeds},
                         model=models, phase_records=records, calc_opts={"pdens": 1000})
        # Keep extraction and validity criteria identical to independent checks.
        from rutile3.engines.binary import extract_point
        for index, x in enumerate(seeds):
            point = eq.isel({"X_"+settings["components"][1]: index}).squeeze(drop=True)
            instances, valid = extract_point(point, settings["components"], x)
            if not valid:
                retried += 1
                try:
                    retry = equilibrium(db, components, phases,
                                        {v.N: 1, v.P: settings["pressure"], v.T: float(t),
                                         v.X(settings["components"][1]): x}, model=models,
                                        phase_records=records, calc_opts={"pdens": 2000})
                    instances, valid = extract_point(retry.squeeze(drop=True), settings["components"], x)
                except Exception:
                    valid = False
                if not valid:
                    failures.append({"temperature": float(t), "mole_fraction": x,
                                     "error": "Boundary seed unresolved after individual pdens=2000 retry"})
                    continue

The form defaults to **Auto** temperature range. Before boundary mapping, a
cancellable worker preflight checks 10 equally spaced overall mole fractions
across the binary, using 1e-6 and 1−1e-6 at the endpoints for numerical stability.
It heats each probe until it is fully liquid (non-liquid molar fraction ≤1e-6),
then bisects its last-solid/fully-liquid bracket to 0.25 K. The upper plot limit
uses the highest upper bracket edge plus 30 K, rounded upward to a whole kelvin
where allowed by documented limits. A final equilibrium check confirms liquid at
all 10 probes at that upper limit. The lower limit is 300 K, or the documented
assessment minimum if higher. **Manual limits** remain available.

The search is bounded by the selected source's documented temperature limits and
the app's 6,000 K maximum, reserving room for the 30 K margin. Source selection
defers the unknown temperature range until the worker resolves and checks it;
pressure, composition, and model compatibility checks still apply before launch.
Missing LIQUID models, unresolved equilibria, or a missing liquid bracket produce
an explicit error asking for Manual mode. There is no arbitrary temperature
fallback. An already-liquid probe only bounds melting below the graph floor.

Auto estimates the **liquidus**, not the onset of melting or a solidification
history. Normal melting on heating is assumed; ten probes can miss narrow maxima

"""TDB parsing and pycalphad model inspection."""
from pycalphad import Database, Model, variables as v
from pycalphad.core.utils import filter_phases


def parse_tdb(raw):
    try:
        content = raw.decode("utf-8-sig")
    except UnicodeDecodeError:
        content = raw.decode("cp1252")
    return Database(content.replace("\r\n", "\n").replace("\r", "\n"))


def available_phases(db, components):
    comps = list(components) + (["VA"] if "VA" in db.elements else [])
    phases = sorted(filter_phases(db, comps))
    energetic = {p["phase_name"] for p in db._parameters.all() if p["parameter_type"] == "G"}
    return [p for p in phases if p in energetic], comps


def solver_models(db, components, phases):
    """Remove only exact copies of a linked model's disordered contribution.

    A partitioned ordered model already includes its disordered state. Some
    assessments additionally define an identical standalone phase. Letting both
    compete creates degenerate phase identities. Never infer equivalence by name
    or sampled energy: require matching constitutions and symbolic GM equality.
    """
    models = {p: Model(db, components, p) for p in phases}
    excluded = []
    for ordered in phases:
        hints = db.phases[ordered].model_hints
        base = hints.get("disordered_phase")
        if not base or hints.get("ordered_phase") != ordered or base == ordered:
            continue
        reference = Model(db, components, base)
        for name in list(models):
            if name == ordered or db.phases[name].model_hints.get("ordered_phase"):
                continue
            candidate = models[name]
            if candidate.constituents != reference.constituents or candidate.site_ratios != reference.site_ratios:
                continue
            rename = {sf: v.SiteFraction(base, sf.sublattice_index, sf.species)
                      for sf in candidate.site_fractions}
            if candidate.GM.xreplace(rename) == reference.GM:
                excluded.append({"phase": name, "represented_by": ordered, "disordered_model": base,
                                 "reason": "Exact symbolic duplicate of the linked disordered Gibbs-energy model"})
                del models[name]
    return models, excluded

    db = parse_tdb(raw)
    types, interactions = set(), {}
    for parameter in db._parameters.all():
        family = parameter["parameter_type"]
        types.add(family)
        elements = sorted({element for sublattice in parameter["constituent_array"]
                           for species in sublattice for element in species.constituents
                           if element in db.elements and element not in {"VA", "/-"}})
        if len(elements) > 1:
            by_family = interactions.setdefault("-".join(elements), {})
            by_family.setdefault(family, set()).add(parameter["phase_name"])
    if not db.elements:
        raise ValueError("No elements were parsed.")
    families = {
        "thermodynamic": {"G"},
        "mobility": {"MQ", "MF", "DQ", "DF"},
        "volume": {"V0", "VA", "VK", "VC", "VS"},

cancellable worker preflight checks 10 equally spaced overall mole fractions
across the binary, using 1e-6 and 1−1e-6 at the endpoints for numerical stability.
It heats each probe until it is fully liquid (non-liquid molar fraction ≤1e-6),
then bisects its last-solid/fully-liquid bracket to 0.25 K. The upper plot limit
uses the highest upper bracket edge plus 30 K, rounded upward to a whole kelvin
where allowed by documented limits. A final equilibrium check confirms liquid at
all 10 probes at that upper limit. The lower limit is 300 K, or the documented
assessment minimum if higher. **Manual limits** remain available.

The search is bounded by the selected source's documented temperature limits and
the app's 6,000 K maximum, reserving room for the 30 K margin. Source selection
defers the unknown temperature range until the worker resolves and checks it;
pressure, composition, and model compatibility checks still apply before launch.
Missing LIQUID models, unresolved equilibria, or a missing liquid bracket produce
an explicit error asking for Manual mode. There is no arbitrary temperature
fallback. An already-liquid probe only bounds melting below the graph floor.

from pathlib import Path
from time import perf_counter
import numpy as np
from pycalphad import calculate, equilibrium, variables as v
from pycalphad.codegen.phase_record_factory import PhaseRecordFactory
from rutile3.engines.tdb import parse_tdb, available_phases, solver_models
from rutile3.engines.boundaries import lower_energy_hull
from rutile3.engines.binary import extract_row

for path, pair, ts in [(Path("examples/AlCu-21Kro.tdb"), ["AL","CU"], [1300,1357,1358,1388]),
                      (next(Path("workspace/imports").glob("*/PtSi-08Xu.tdb")), ["PT","SI"], [1132.6875,1687,2030,2042,2043,2073])]:
    db=parse_tdb(path.read_bytes()); phases, active=available_phases(db,pair)
    models,_=solver_models(db,active,phases); records=PhaseRecordFactory(db,active,[v.N,v.P,v.T],models)
    for t in ts:
        start=perf_counter()
        points=calculate(db,active,sorted(models),N=1,P=101325,T=t,model=models,phase_records=records,pdens=1000,output="GM")
        xs=points.X.sel(component=pair[1]).values.ravel()
        gs=points.GM.values.ravel()
        names=points.Phase.values.ravel()
        hull=lower_energy_hull(xs,gs)
        print(pair,t,"time",round(perf_counter()-start,3),"hull",len(hull),"bounds",min(xs),max(xs),
              "nonliquid",[(p,round(min(x),8),round(max(x),8),len(x)) for p in sorted(set(names[hull])-{"LIQUID"})
                           if len(x:=xs[hull][names[hull]==p])],flush=True)
        if t == 1132.6875:
            for density in (1000,2000,4000):
                probes=np.clip(np.linspace(0,1,10),1e-6,1-1e-6)
                eq=equilibrium(db,active,sorted(models),{v.N:1,v.P:101325,v.T:t,v.X(pair[1]):probes},
                               model=models,phase_records=records,calc_opts={"pdens":density})
                print(density,[(round(x,6),valid,[p["phase"] for p in phases]) for x,(phases,valid) in zip(probes,extract_row(eq,pair,probes))])

import os
from pathlib import Path
import socket
import subprocess
import sys
import time

import requests
from playwright.sync_api import sync_playwright


def main():
    root = Path.cwd()
    output = root / "workspace" / "auto-temperature-check"
    output.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    with socket.socket() as sock:
        sock.bind(("127.0.0.1", 0))
        port = sock.getsockname()[1]
    base = f"http://127.0.0.1:{port}"
    env = dict(os.environ, RUTILE_WORKSPACE=str(output), RUTILE_CATALOG_PATH=str(output / "catalog.sqlite3"), RUTILE_TEST_URL=base)
    with (output / "server.log").open("w") as log:
        server = subprocess.Popen([sys.executable, "scripts/run_app.py", "--port", str(port)],
                                  env=env, stdout=log, stderr=log, creationflags=subprocess.CREATE_NO_WINDOW)
        try:
            for _ in range(120):
                try:
                    if requests.get(base, timeout=1).ok:
                        break
                except requests.RequestException:
                    time.sleep(.25)
            else:
                raise AssertionError("Server startup timed out")
            subprocess.run([sys.executable, "scripts/check_plot_ui.py"], env=env, check=True)
            with sync_playwright() as playwright:
                browser = playwright.chromium.launch(channel="msedge", headless=True)
                page = browser.new_page(viewport={"width":1440, "height":810}, reduced_motion="reduce")
                errors = []
                page.on("pageerror", lambda error: errors.append(str(error)))
                page.goto(base)
                assert not page.locator(".wordmark").count()
                page.get_by_role("button", name="Start", exact=True).click()
                page.locator("#menu-diagrams").click()
                pt_si = next((root / "workspace" / "imports").glob("*/PtSi-08Xu.tdb"))
                for path, expected in [(root/"examples"/"AlCu-21Kro.tdb", 1388), (pt_si, 2072)]:
                    page.locator("#upload").set_input_files(path)
                    page.locator("#calculation-settings > summary").click()
                    page.locator("#resolution").select_option("31,25")
                    page.locator("#calculation-settings > summary").click()
                    with page.expect_response(lambda r: r.url.endswith("/api/diagrams")) as response:
                        page.locator("#calculate").click()
                    job = response.value.json()["id"]
                    assert page.locator(".calculation-steps").is_visible()
                    assert not page.locator("#progress").count()
                    page.wait_for_function("['complete','interrupted'].includes(document.querySelector('#workspace').dataset.stage)", timeout=180_000)
                    assert page.locator("#workspace").get_attribute("data-stage") == "complete", page.locator("#status").inner_text()
                    result = page.request.get(f"{base}/api/jobs/{job}/result").json()
                    assert result["settings"]["temperature_max"] == expected
                    estimate = result["provenance"]["temperature_range_estimate"]
                    assert estimate["hull_screening"]["slices"] >= 2
                    assert len(result["cells"]) == 775
                    print(path.name, "top", expected, "method", result["boundaries"]["method"],
                          "checks", result["validation"]["counts"], "preflight retries", estimate["equilibrium_retries"])
                    page.screenshot(path=output/f"{path.stem}.png")
                    page.wait_for_timeout(400)
                assert not errors, errors
        finally:
            server.terminate()
            server.wait(timeout=10)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

import runpy, math
from pycalphad import calculate,equilibrium,variables as v
from rutile3.engines.tdb import parse_tdb,available_phases,solver_models
from rutile3.engines.boundaries import lower_energy_hull
from rutile3.engines.temperature import estimate_temperature_range
base=runpy.run_path('backend/tests/test_temperature.py')['IDEAL_MELTING']
slope=10+8.3145*math.log(2)+(25200-15000)/2400
raw=base+f"""
PHASE COMPOUND % 2 1 1 !
CONSTITUENT COMPOUND :AL:CU: !
PARAMETER G(COMPOUND,AL:CU;0) 1 50400-{2*slope:.10f}*T; 6000 N !
""".encode()
db=parse_tdb(raw); phases,components=available_phases(db,['AL','CU']); models,_=solver_models(db,components,phases)
print(phases, models['COMPOUND'].GM)
for t in [2000,2200,2300,2380,2390,2399,2400,2401]:
    grid=calculate(db,components,phases,T=t,P=101325,N=1,output="GM",pdens=1000)
    xs=grid.X.sel(component='CU').values.ravel(); ys=grid.GM.values.ravel(); names=grid.Phase.values.ravel()
    h=lower_energy_hull(xs,ys)
    eq=equilibrium(db,components,phases,{v.N:1,v.P:101325,v.T:t,v.X('CU'):[.5,.555555555]},calc_opts={"pdens":1000})
    print(t,set(names[h]), eq.Phase.values.reshape(2,-1),eq.NP.values.reshape(2,-1))
result=estimate_temperature_range(raw,{"components":["AL","CU"],"pressure":101325}, lambda _:None)
print(result)

content.text:
Removed the JoelTech footer from every page and the redundant phase-diagram progress bar. The JT startup animation and counted stage fills are still there. The tracking marker now fades as soon as you hover over a label. When you leave the label, it moves to the pointer before fading back in. A pinned point stays fixed during a drag.

**Auto temperature.** Pt–Si failed because one equilibrium probe at 1132.69 K didn’t converge. Auto now retries unresolved points at twice the sampling density. It also screens the Gibbs-energy hull across composition for higher liquidus peaks between the ten fixed probes, then checks any candidates with equilibrium solves before adding the 30 K margin. This can catch narrow peaks, though finite sampling can still miss them.

Both Auto runs completed in Edge. The imported **Pt–Si** assessment now reaches **2072 K**. The bundled **Al–Cu** assessment reaches **1388 K**, the same Auto limit I reproduced before the change. Its saved Manual runs at **1200 K** cut off the copper-rich liquidus near **1358 K**.

**Do higher settings improve the lines?** Yes. Both runs used the **convex-hull fallback**. The hull finds candidate regions, pycalphad solves the coexistence points, and the plot connects those points. Rutile tries pycalphad’s boundary continuation first. Higher quality uses smaller continuation steps or tighter fallback refinement, and runs more independent checks. That can resolve finer features, while coverage still depends on which equilibria converge. [pycalphad mapping documentation](https://pycalphad.org/docs/latest/examples/1_Phase_Diagrams/3_Mapping.html)

All 111 tests passed, including a regression for a liquidus peak between the fixed probes.
